vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: clawd-zero-trust
Version: 1.3.2

The clawd-zero-trust bundle is a comprehensive security hardening framework for OpenClaw deployments. It implements legitimate security controls including DNS-based egress filtering via UFW (egress-filter.sh), plugin integrity monitoring using SHA-256 hashing (plugin-integrity.sh), and Principle of Least Privilege (PLP) tool scoping (plp-config.sh). While the scripts require root privileges and modify system firewall rules, these actions are strictly aligned with the stated purpose of Zero Trust architecture. The instructions in SKILL.md regarding update prevention and 'Founder approval' are framed as stability measures to prevent breaking changes and do not exhibit malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized persistence.

llm.summary: This appears to be a real security-hardening skill, but it includes high-impact firewall and OpenClaw execution settings that can weaken the protections it advertises.

dimensions.detail: Root-level UFW mutation is expected for firewall hardening, but hardening.json sets tools.exec to host gateway, security full, ask off, and the egress policy permits unrestricted outbound TCP/443 despite claims of provider-only egress.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No remote payload retrieval or install-time backdoor was found, but the release packager recursively archives the live skill tree without an explicit allowlist or symlink rejection, creating publication-time disclosure risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md contains mandatory update-response instructions and recommends an absolute post-update repair script path that is not included in the artifact, which can steer agent output beyond ordinary skill guidance.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists state under .state, modifies OpenClaw config, changes durable UFW rules, and whitelist.sh permanently appends arbitrary providers before forcing privileged firewall apply; rollback can reset outgoing traffic to permissive allow.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The audit, UFW egress filtering, plugin integrity, and PLP features fit the Zero Trust purpose, but the same package also applies full non-interactive gateway exec, arbitrary dynamic egress additions, and a destination-independent HTTPS rule that conflict with least-privilege claims.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill carefully before installing. Do not run harden.sh --apply or egress-filter.sh --apply as shipped in a sensitive environment until you remove or constrain full non-interactive gateway exec, remove the unrestricted outbound 443 rule, add validation and approval to whitelist.sh, and verify any post-update repair script independently. Treat it as a high-impact administrative tool, not a low-risk advisory skill.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The broader release-gate and packaging functionality is disclosed and adjacent to shipping a security skill, so this is scope expansion rather than standalone evidence of malicious behavior.
[AE1] unexpected: The local artifact contains scripts/egress-filter.sh and it was inspected; the partial-inspection concern is not supported in this adjudication context.
[RA1] unexpected: The self-update section mostly forbids automatic updates, but the adjacent mandatory proposal block still promotes update commands and an unaudited local repair script path, so the concern is partially supported as unsafe steering rather than runtime self-modification.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The mandatory update proposal and the whitelist helper create mismatch with the claimed hardening posture: one steers operators to an unaudited script, and the other advertises secure whitelisting while puncturing the egress policy.
[SDI-1] unexpected: hardening.json materially expands local execution authority with security full and ask off, which is not proportionate to a least-privilege hardening profile without clearer scoping and approvals.
[SDI-2] unexpected: scripts/whitelist.sh accepts arbitrary domain and port values, appends them persistently, and runs sudo egress-filter.sh --apply --force without validation or interactive authorization.
[TM1] expected: The rm -f temp cleanup and numbered UFW rule deletion are expected shell administration patterns; the material issue is not command injection but the privileged policy mutation and force bypass around them.
[TM2] expected: The cited command chaining mostly reflects cleanup and operator recovery instructions; it does not by itself show capability escalation.
[T01] unexpected: The mandatory update format in SKILL.md is supported by artifact evidence and is under-scoped because it pushes a fixed operator command sequence referencing a script outside the reviewed package.
[T05] unexpected: The excessive execution-privilege finding is supported: harden.sh merges hardening.json into openclaw.json, and hardening.json sets gateway exec to full with ask off.
[T09] unexpected: Several coding-practice findings are supported in context: egress-filter.sh allows outbound 443/tcp to any destination, fail-open reset permits outgoing traffic, plugin integrity hashes only one JS entry point, and audit.sh suppresses actionable findings by broad plugin-name patterns.
